title: AZ-aware VPC Connector Terraform Module with Endpoint Guardrails
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Create a reusable Terraform module (vpc-connector) to provision AZ-aware subnets, NAT/IGW egress options, VPC endpoints (Gateway + Interface) and routing guardrails for Redwood Private deployments. The module must support zero-downtime upgrades, automated health checks for network connectivity and endpoint reachability, sensible defaults for security posture, and observability hooks for Console dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes inputs for AZ count, subnet sizing strategy, public/private mapping, and egress mode (single-IGW, NAT gateways per-AZ, or managed NAT gateway pool)
Creates and tags public and private subnets per AZ with route tables and explicit route resources for IGW/NAT depending on selected egress mode
Creates Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB and Interface endpoints for ECR, STS, KMS with optional private-dns and endpoint security groups
Implements route table and endpoint guardrails: disallow default 0.0.0.0/0 on private route tables without explicit IGW/NAT mapping; validate prefix-list usage for service egress
Provides outputs: subnet ids (by AZ and role), route table ids, endpoint ids, recommended security group ids, and a semantic module version output
Includes a non-destructive upgrade path with automated state migration notes and a canary rollout plan for infra changes
Health checks: CloudWatch metrics for endpoint connection latency and failed DNS resolves, and automated Terraform plan-time checks to detect drift
Terratest and/or terraform-validate CI tests run in the pipeline and pass for common deployment permutations
Documentation/README with example usages for Hosted/Dedicated/Private variants and a migration playbook for customers upgrading from legacy vpc modules
tasks: Design module interface and input validation (variables.tf + validations)
Implement resources: vpc, subnets (public/private), route tables, igw, nat gateways, elastic ips, endpoints (gateway & interface)
Add optional helpers: prefix list attachments, route propagation, and explicit route resources for cross-AZ failover
Implement health-checking resources: CloudWatch alarms, metric filters, and a lightweight Lambda (or SSM Automation) for remediation runbooks
Write CI tests (terratest/azure equivalent) and example integration stacks for 2-AZ and 3-AZ topologies
Author upgrade/migration playbook and terraform import mappings for customer states
Add policy checks and pre-apply validations (pre-commit and pipeline job) to prevent unsafe config
Review and security sign-off; prepare module for public consumption in internal module registry
implementation_notes: Prefer one NAT gateway per AZ for predictable cross-AZ egress latency; allow cost-optimized single-NAT option via variable egress_mode
Use aws_vpc_endpoint (gateway) for s3 & dynamodb to avoid egress charges; use aws_vpc_endpoint (interface) for ECR/STS/KMS with security group injection
Expose boolean flags for private_dns_enabled on interface endpoints (default true) but document consequences for split-horizon DNS in private deployments
Tagging schema: redwood:env, redwood:stack, redwood:component, cost_center; ensure tags are applied to all created resources
Provide built-in guardrail validations to fail plan if: private subnet has 0.0.0.0/0 route without declared egress_mode, or interface endpoint security groups are overly permissive
Plan to publish module to internal registry with semantic versioning; maintain migration notes in CHANGELOG.md
Observability: emit CloudWatch metrics via custom namespace (Redwood/VPCConnector) for endpoint_health and route_drift; wire metrics to Console via exporter/collection job
For automated repairs, prefer runbook steps surfaced to SRE instead of full auto-remediation for initial rollout; add optional auto-remediate flag for low-risk fixes
